data.name: Circle of Shapers
data.lead:
> **The Circle of Shapers at a Glance**
>
> You **Shape the Land**. As a Bonus Action, spend a use of Wild Shape to raise a rampart for cover, lift a pillar under a friend or a foe, or turn the ground into grasping roots and stone. It lasts an hour, and from 6th level your Bonus Action can rework it for free every turn after: walk the wall forward, move the grasp, raise the pillar higher. Out of a fight the same power builds.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | The Mason's Hand | shape stone, earth, and wood with your hands like clay | Level 3 |
> | Shape the Land | Wild Shape turned outward: rampart, pillar, or grasp | Level 3 |
> | Raise the Works | build walls, bridges, and rooms with your party; rework your shapings as a Bonus Action | Level 6 |
> | Living Stone | two shapings at once; a rampart when an ally is hit; your works keep growing | Level 10 |
> | What Stands | the stone answers faster; what you build stays | Level 14 |
>
> **What it looks like:** the spell goes off, and the ground answers in the same breath: a rampart rises between the archers and your wizard, a pillar lifts your rogue onto the high ground, or the earth closes on the brute's ankles where your fighter wants him. From 6th level the ground keeps changing, turn after turn.

**Wild Shape is still yours.** You can take a beast's shape as any druid can; the uses are one pool.

features.name: Circle of Shapers Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of Shapers Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Druid Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Floating Disk*, *Spike Growth* |
| 5 | *Meld into Stone*, *Plant Growth* |
| 7 | *Stone Shape*, *Stoneskin* |
| 9 | *Tree Stride*, *Wall of Stone* |

features.name: The Mason's Hand
features.text: You can shape unworked stone, earth, or wood with your bare hands as if it were wet clay: up to a 1-foot cube a minute, and it holds its new shape when you let go. Stones you join this way fit with no mortar and no gap. You also know at a touch whether a wall, a bridge, or a mine's ceiling is sound, and where it will fail first. Masons' lodges, quarrymen, and dry-stone wallers know you for one of their own after a look at your hands: given an evening among them, you can find a bed and hear who is building what, and who isn't paying.

features.name: Shape the Land
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to shape the ground at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Choose one shaping. It lasts for 1 hour or until you dismiss it (no action required). If you make a shaping while you already have as many as you can maintain (one, or two from Living Stone), your oldest shaping ends. Earth, stone, and roots answer you; worked stone floors and wooden decks answer too, but slowly: a shaping there takes effect at the start of your next turn, and they rejoin when the shaping ends.

- *Rampart.* Up to three 5-foot sections of earth or stone wall rise in unoccupied spaces, each 5 feet wide and 5 feet high; each must touch another section or the point you chose. A section is a solid block: nothing moves through it, it can be climbed, and it can stand on top of another section. A single section is chest-high to a Medium creature: it gives Half Cover to a creature behind it, or Three-Quarters Cover if that creature is Small or has the Prone condition. Two sections stacked, 10 feet high, block line of sight and give Total Cover to a Large or smaller creature behind them. Each section has AC 15 and Hit Points equal to twice your Druid level. The sections can instead lie flat, end to end, as a span or a stair up to 15 feet long, which bears any weight a stone bridge would.
- *Pillar.* A 5-foot column rises up to 15 feet under a Medium or smaller creature or an empty space. It stops when the column, or a creature on it, would touch a ceiling, so it never crushes a rider. A willing creature rides it up safely. An unwilling creature makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC; on a failed save it's lifted, and on a success it steps off into an adjacent space of its choice. A creature on top can climb down the sides, or step off and fall. The column has AC 15 and Hit Points equal to twice your Druid level, as a Rampart section has; if it's destroyed, a creature on top falls.
- *Grasp.* The ground in a 15-foot-radius circle turns to roots and grinding stone. It's Difficult Terrain for creatures you don't choose. For the first minute, the roots also grasp: when such a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it makes a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or has the Restrained condition until the start of its next turn. A Huge or larger creature is too big to hold, and so is a Large one until you reach Druid level 6; for it, the Grasp is only Difficult Terrain.

You can use this feature once without expending a use of Wild Shape. You regain this free use when you finish a Short or Long Rest. From Druid level 10, you can spend it on The Wall Comes Up instead.

**Out of a fight**, the same shapings build: a rampart is a wall for a camp, a pillar is a lookout or a stair, a grasp holds a riverbank from flooding. Shapings you make outside combat can be any shape that fits their size.

features.name: Raise the Works
features.text:
You can build. With 10 minutes of work, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to raise a structure of earth, stone, or wood: a wall up to 30 feet long and 10 feet high, a bridge spanning up to 5 feet per Druid level, a stair, or a room with walls and a roof that fits in a 20-foot cube. Each 5-foot section has the AC and Hit Points of a Rampart section. It lasts until you finish your next Long Rest, then settles back into the ground.

Building is loud and plain to see: the ground groans, and anyone within a mile who is looking knows where you are. It needn't be lonely work. Each creature that helps you for the full 10 minutes (hauling, bracing, singing the stone along) adds 10 feet to the length of a wall or the span of a bridge.

**Rework.** The land keeps answering once it has moved. As a Bonus Action, you can rework one of your shapings from Shape the Land within 60 feet of yourself without expending a use: sink your Rampart's sections and raise them in new spaces (or lay them flat farther along), raise or lower your Pillar by up to 15 feet, or move your Grasp up to 15 feet. A creature that a moved Grasp reaches isn't held until it starts its turn there. Reworking a shaping doesn't lengthen it, or the Grasp's first minute.

features.name: Living Stone
features.text:
You can maintain two shapings from Shape the Land at once.

**The Wall Comes Up.** When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend a use of your Wild Shape feature (or your free use from Shape the Land) and raise a single Rampart section in an unoccupied space between it and the attacker. If there is no such space, as against an attacker within 5 feet, the stone rises along the edge of the creature's own space and occupies no space. The creature has Half Cover against that attack, which can turn the hit into a miss. The section lasts for 1 minute and doesn't count against the shapings you can maintain.

**Works That Grow.** A structure you raise with Raise the Works mends itself: it regains all its Hit Points at dawn, and damage to it closes like a wound.

features.name: What Stands
features.text:
When you roll Initiative and have fewer than two uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one. In addition, your Rampart sections have AC 17 and Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

**Permanence.** A structure you raise with Raise the Works, and keep raising for seven days in a row, stays when its time is up. It's as permanent as stone. It's yours, and the land remembers who asked for it.

> **Playing a Shaper**
>
> Your Wild Shape uses are what the land will give you between rests, and the field is your canvas. A rampart that rises before the archers loose is a wall; one that rises after is only a heap of earth. From 6th level, keep the canvas moving: every turn after, your Bonus Action reworks a shaping for free. Walk the rampart forward with your fighter, slide the grasp onto the ones who stepped out of it, take your rogue up another 15 feet. In a chase, lay the rampart flat as a span over the gap, and rework it ahead of your runner each turn. From 10th, the ground can rise between a friend and the blade the moment they're hit, if the land still has a use to give you. Out of a fight, you're the party's engineer: the bridge, the wall, the safe room in the cliff, and everyone who helps makes it bigger.

features.name: Earth Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Earth Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Sorcerer Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Shield*, *Spike Growth* |
| 5 | *Fireball*, *Meld into Stone* |
| 7 | *Stone Shape*, *Stoneskin* |
| 9 | *Conjure Elemental*, *Wall of Stone* |

features.name: The Mark
features.text: You always know which way is down and how deep you are underground. While your Pressure is 3, the ground within 5 feet of you trembles and loose stones rattle. As a Bonus Action, you can crack or seal a seam in unworked stone or earth you touch, up to a 1-foot cube.

features.name: Bury
features.text: Your Release is heavy. The creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet for each Pressure you spent, until the start of your next turn. If you spent 3 Pressure, it also has the Prone condition unless it is Huge or larger.

features.name: Bedrock
features.text: This is your stance (The Plane Coming Through): you harden into the mountain. While hardened, you can't be moved against your will or knocked Prone, and you have a +1 bonus to AC.

features.name: Under the Mountain
features.text:
*Also at this level: Discipline, and a d6 Release die (2d6 from Sorcerer level 8).*

You have Tremorsense out to 30 feet, and Resistance to Fire damage. While you are hardened, you have a Burrow Speed equal to half your Speed through sand, earth, and loose stone, leaving no tunnel.

**Ore-Sense.** By touching the ground for 1 minute, you know whether any metal ore lies within 500 feet of you, which metals, and roughly where.

features.name: Upheaval
features.text:
*Also at this level: On Purpose.*

When you Release with 3 Pressure, the ground in a 10-foot radius around the creature heaves: it becomes Difficult Terrain until the start of your next turn, and each other creature of your choice in that area makes a Strength saving throw against your Sorcerer spell save DC or has the Prone condition. If you chose molten, the area burns instead of heaving: a creature that enters it or starts its turn there takes Fire damage equal to one roll of your Release die.

**Stone-Reader.** By touching worked stone, you know when it was cut and laid, and whether anything is hidden in it or behind it.

features.name: Cataclysm
features.text: This is your Detonation (The Plane Coming Through). Once per Long Rest, when you Overflow on purpose, you can make it a 30-foot Emanation, and each creature that fails its saving throw is also Buried as if you had Released 3 Pressure on it.

features.name: Fire Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Fire Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Sorcerer Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Burning Hands*, *Scorching Ray* |
| 5 | *Fireball*, *Fly* |
| 7 | *Fire Shield*, *Wall of Fire* |
| 9 | *Conjure Elemental*, *Flame Strike* |

features.name: The Mark
features.text: Mundane heat doesn't trouble you: hot weather, a hot coal in your hand, the air above a forge. While your Pressure is 3, your mark glows through clothing and smoke curls off your skin. As a Bonus Action, you can light a flammable object you touch that isn't being worn or carried, or snuff out a nonmagical flame no larger than a campfire within 30 feet of yourself.

features.name: Kindle
features.text:
Your Release doesn't hit all at once; it catches. When you Release, the creature takes no Release damage then. It is Kindled instead:

1. **Set the burn dice.** Put a number of Release dice beside the creature on the table, equal to the Pressure you spent. These are its burn dice.
2. **Burn.** At the start of each of the creature's turns, you roll its burn dice, and it takes that much Fire damage.
3. **Burn down.** After each roll, take one burn die away. When the last die is gone, the fire is out.

**One Fire at a Time.** A creature burns with only one Kindle. If you Kindle a creature that is already burning, compare the new burn dice with the dice it has now. If the new Kindle has more, it replaces the old one. If it has the same number or fewer, the creature takes your Release damage at once, as from an ordinary Release, and its fire is unchanged.

**While It Burns.** The creature sheds Bright Light in a 5-foot radius and can't hide. The fire also goes out when the creature, or another creature within 5 feet of it, takes an action to put it out, or when the creature is submerged in water.

features.name: Wreathed
features.text: This is your stance (The Plane Coming Through): you wreathe yourself in fire. While wreathed, you shed Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet, and a creature that touches you or hits you with a melee attack roll takes Fire damage equal to your Charisma modifier.

features.name: Burning Bright
features.text:
*Also at this level: Discipline, and a d6 Release die (2d6 from Sorcerer level 8).*

You have Resistance to Fire damage, and Fire damage from your Sorcerer spells and your Kindle ignores Resistance. While you are wreathed, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

**Forge-Hand.** You can heat metal or glass you hold to working temperature over 10 minutes, and keep it there as long as you hold it. For work with Smith's Tools, Glassblower's Tools, Jeweler's Tools, or Cook's Utensils, you count as a forge, a furnace, or an oven.

features.name: Wildfire
features.text:
*Also at this level: On Purpose.*

When a Kindled creature drops to 0 Hit Points, its fire leaps: one creature of your choice within 15 feet of it becomes Kindled with the burn dice it had left.

**Ash-Reader.** By touching the remains of a fire, you know how long ago it burned (to the hour, if within the last week), what fed it, and whether it was set or caught, and by a sorcerer or not.

features.name: Inferno
features.text: This is your Detonation (The Plane Coming Through). Once per Long Rest, when you Overflow on purpose, you can make it a 30-foot Emanation, and each creature that fails its saving throw is also Kindled with three burn dice.

features.name: Frost Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Frost Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Sorcerer Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Hold Person*, *Ice Knife* |
| 5 | *Sleet Storm*, *Slow* |
| 7 | *Fire Shield*, *Ice Storm* |
| 9 | *Cone of Cold*, *Conjure Elemental* |

features.name: The Mark
features.text: Mundane cold doesn't trouble you. While your Pressure is 3, frost forms on whatever you touch and your breath shows. As a Bonus Action, you can freeze nonmagical water you can see within 30 feet of yourself, up to a 10-foot Cube, solid enough to walk on; it thaws normally.

features.name: Freeze
features.text: When you Release, the creature's Speed decreases by 10 feet for each Pressure you spent, and it can't take Reactions, until the start of your next turn. If you spent 3 Pressure, it also makes a Constitution saving throw against your Sorcerer spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Rime
features.text: This is your stance (The Plane Coming Through): you skin yourself in rime. When you take it, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down), which last until the stance ends. While rimed, a creature that hits you with a melee attack roll has its Speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn: the cold gets into its joints.

features.name: Hoarfrost
features.text:
*Also at this level: Discipline, and a d6 Release die (2d6 from Sorcerer level 8).*

You have Resistance to Cold damage, and Cold damage from your Sorcerer spells ignores Resistance. When you Release, the ground in a 10-foot radius around the creature also becomes Difficult Terrain until the start of your next turn. While rimed, you can walk across water as if it were solid ground, freezing it under each step (it thaws behind you), and ice and snow are never Difficult Terrain for you.

**Icehouse.** Once per Long Rest, you can spend 10 minutes chilling a closed space no larger than a 10-foot Cube: a cellar, a cask, a ship's hold, a sickroom. For 24 hours it stays as cold as a winter cellar, whatever the weather outside. Food kept there doesn't spoil, and anyone resting there is comfortable in any heat.

features.name: Frozen Solid
features.text:
*Also at this level: On Purpose.*

When you Release with 3 Pressure, the creature doesn't make the saving throw against Freeze; it has the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn.

**Ice-Reader.** You know at a glance how thick any ice you can see is, and whether it will bear a given weight: a person, a cart, a cannon, an army.

features.name: Absolute Zero
features.text: This is your Detonation (The Plane Coming Through). Once per Long Rest, when you Overflow on purpose, you can make it a 30-foot Emanation, and each creature that fails its saving throw also has the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Kinetic Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Kinetic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Sorcerer Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Levitate*, *Magic Missile* |
| 5 | *Haste*, *Tiny Hut* |
| 7 | *Dimension Door*, *Resilient Sphere* |
| 9 | *Arcane Hand*, *Telekinesis* |

features.name: The Mark
features.text: While your Pressure is 3, loose objects within 5 feet of you rattle and drift. As a Bonus Action, you can push or pull an unattended object weighing up to 10 pounds that you can see within 30 feet of yourself, up to 10 feet.

features.name: Impressed Force
features.text:
When you Release, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from you for each Pressure you spent. If you spent 3 Pressure, it also has the Prone condition.

Or you can take the push yourself: instead of moving the creature, you fly up to 10 feet for each Pressure you spent, in a straight line, without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If you end in the air, you fall. The Release dice still land, but the creature isn't pushed or knocked Prone.

features.name: Equal and Opposite
features.text: This is your stance (The Plane Coming Through): you brace yourself inside your own push. While braced, when an attack roll hits you, the damage is reduced by half your Charisma modifier (round up, minimum of 1), and if the attacker is within 5 feet of you, you can push it up to 5 feet straight away from you (no action required).

features.name: Deflection
features.text:
*Also at this level: Discipline, and a d6 Release die (2d6 from Sorcerer level 8).*

You have Resistance to Force damage, and when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is hit by an attack roll, you can take a Reaction and spend all your Pressure (at least 1) to reduce the damage by a roll of that many Release dice. You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. While braced, you have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, you can climb across ceilings with your hands free, and you take no damage from falling.

**Porter.** Your carrying capacity is doubled, and you can steady anything you carry or hold: it doesn't spill, slosh, or swing, however you move.

features.name: Pin
features.text:
*Also at this level: On Purpose.*

When you Release with 3 Pressure, the creature also makes a Strength saving throw against your Sorcerer spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn, pinned where it lies.

**Feel the Load.** By touching a floor, beam, bridge, wall, or vault, you know whether it will bear a given weight, and where it's weakest.

features.name: Shockwave
features.text: This is your Detonation (The Plane Coming Through). Once per Long Rest, when you Overflow on purpose, you can make it a 30-foot Emanation, and each creature that fails its saving throw is also pushed up to 10 feet straight away from you and has the Prone condition. You can instead give any of those creatures the Restrained condition until the start of your next turn, as with Pin.

features.name: Light Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Light Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Sorcerer Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Faerie Fire*, *Guiding Bolt* |
| 5 | *Daylight*, *Hypnotic Pattern* |
| 7 | *Greater Invisibility*, *Guardian of Faith* |
| 9 | *Dispel Evil and Good*, *Hallow* |

features.name: The Mark
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can make your mark shed Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet, or stop it. While your Pressure is 3, it sheds Dim Light in a 5-foot radius whether you want it to or not.

features.name: Illuminate
features.text: When you Release, until the start of your next turn the creature sheds Dim Light in a 5-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition, and the next attack roll against it has Advantage. If you spent 2 or more Pressure, every attack roll against it has Advantage instead. If you spent 3 Pressure, it also makes a Constitution saving throw against your Sorcerer spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Blaze
features.text: This is your stance (The Plane Coming Through): your mark blazes. While blazing, you shed Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet, and when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack roll, the glare takes it full in the face: it has Disadvantage on its other attack rolls this turn.

features.name: Nothing Hidden
features.text:
*Also at this level: Discipline, and a d6 Release die (2d6 from Sorcerer level 8).*

You have Resistance to Radiant damage. While your Pressure is 1 or more, you can see creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition within 10 feet of yourself. Undead and Fiends have Disadvantage on the saving throw against Illuminate. While blazing, once on each of your turns you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see in Bright Light, spending that much movement: you go where the light goes.

**Palimpsest.** By the light of your mark, you can read writing that has been scraped, washed, or faded from a page, see a document's watermark and every correction under its ink, and tell a new forgery from an old letter.

features.name: Searing
features.text:
*Also at this level: On Purpose.*

Illuminate's Blinded condition needs only 2 Pressure, not 3, and Radiant damage from your Sorcerer spells ignores Resistance.

**The Halo.** When you let your mark shed Bright Light, the devout of any faith who see it take you for something holy until you give them reason not to. While the light lasts, you have Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks to calm, sway, or be believed by a crowd.

features.name: Dawn
features.text: This is your Detonation (The Plane Coming Through). Once per Long Rest, when you Overflow on purpose, you can make it a 30-foot Emanation, and each creature that fails its saving throw is also lit as by an Illuminate of 3 Pressure (until the start of your next turn it sheds Dim Light in a 5-foot radius, can't benefit from the Invisible condition, and every attack roll against it has Advantage) and has the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Storm Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Storm Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Sorcerer Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Shatter*, *Thunderwave* |
| 5 | *Call Lightning*, *Lightning Bolt* |
| 7 | *Conjure Minor Elementals*, *Ice Storm* |
| 9 | *Conjure Elemental*, *Hold Monster* |

features.name: The Mark
features.text: You can always tell what the weather will do in the next 24 hours where you are. While your Pressure is 3, your hair lifts, sparks snap from your fingers to metal, and the air smells of a struck bell. When you speak, you can make your voice carry up to 300 feet.

features.name: Forked Strike
features.text: When you Release, the strike jumps. For each Pressure you spent beyond the first, one other creature of your choice within 30 feet of the target (a different creature each time) takes half the Release damage. Roll the Release dice once for all of them.

features.name: Stormcharged
features.text: This is your stance (The Plane Coming Through): you take on the charge before the strike. While charged, your Speed increases by 10 feet, and your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks: you're gone before the blow lands.

features.name: Thunderclap
features.text:
*Also at this level: Discipline, and a d6 Release die (2d6 from Sorcerer level 8).*

You have Resistance to Lightning and Thunder damage, and when a creature within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to Release on it: spend all your Pressure (at least 1), and it takes a number of Release dice of Thunder damage equal to the Pressure you spent, and you can push it up to 10 feet straight away from you. This counts as your one Release for the turn. It doesn't need a spell, and it doesn't set off Forked Strike. While charged, you have a Fly Speed equal to half your Speed, though you fall if you end your turn in the air.

**Wind-Knots.** During a Long Rest, you can tie up to three knots in a cord, and give it to someone else. Whoever unties a knot before your next Long Rest gets a fair wind: for 1 hour, a sailing ship or boat they're aboard moves as though the wind were behind it, whatever the weather. Untied after your next Long Rest, a knot does nothing.

features.name: Eye of the Storm
features.text:
*Also at this level: On Purpose.*

You have a Fly Speed of 60 feet and can hover, and your Forked Strike jumps once for every Pressure you spend, not only those beyond the first.

**Spark-Sense.** You can feel current. By touching an object, you know whether it holds a charge of lightning or carries current, and whether a Mutapan device is running, failing, or about to fail.

features.name: Superstorm
features.text: This is your Detonation (The Plane Coming Through). Once per Long Rest, when you Overflow on purpose, you can make it a 30-foot Emanation, and each creature that fails its saving throw also has the Deafened condition until the start of your next turn and is pushed up to 10 feet straight away from you.

data.name: Envoy Patron
data.lead:
*Every Heaven Sends Its Messengers*

You have made a pact with an angel: a being of the tier that gods send when they want something done. In exchange for your service, you can call on that tier yourself. Your angels come in bursts. Each lands, does one errand, and returns; it has a busy eternity ahead of it.

> **The Envoy at a Glance**
>
> You **Call an Angel**. As a Bonus Action, spend a Pact Magic slot: an angel lands beside the fight, does one errand, and leaves.
>
> - **Strike:** it attacks a creature you name for two of its turns, or until that creature drops.
> - **Guard:** it stays beside an ally (or you), takes the hits meant for them, and catches them if they fall.
> - **Mend:** it carries a store of healing and spends it on your friends.
> - **Bear:** it carries a message or a small thing up to a mile, within the minute.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | Call an Angel | the angel and its errand | Level 3 |
> | Tongue of Fire | Celestial; the names and ranks of the messengers | Level 3 |
> | Messenger | *Sending* borne by an angel; the protocol of any court | Level 6 |
> | Greater Angels | brighter angels; a Strike angel finds a new target, and a Guard angel has Resistance to all damage; the hospitality owed to angels | Level 10 |
> | Archangel | once per Long Rest, an archangel that flattens and frightens; a weekly visitation; the ladder between the heavens | Level 14 |
>
> **What it looks like:** you speak the name and the angel is there beside you, and while your *Eldritch Blast* is still crossing the room it is already moving, right behind it.

features.name: Envoy Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Envoy Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Warlock Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Aid*, *Bless*, *Command*, *Zone of Truth* |
| 5 | *Beacon of Hope*, *Revivify* |
| 7 | *Death Ward*, *Guardian of Faith* |
| 9 | *Commune*, *Flame Strike* |

features.name: Call an Angel
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to call an angel to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. It uses the Angel stat block below, at the row of the Angel table for your Warlock level.

When you call it, give the angel one **errand**:

- **Strike.** Name a creature you can see. The angel attacks it, and departs at the end of its second turn or when the creature drops to 0 Hit Points, whichever comes first: either way, its errand is done. If the creature drops before the angel's first turn, you can name another (no action required), so the angel never leaves without striking.
- **Guard.** Name a creature you can see; you can name yourself. The angel stays close to it and takes the hits meant for it (its Intercede Reaction). When that creature moves, the angel moves with it (no action required), staying within 5 feet of it. If the creature falls, the angel bears it down: it takes no damage from the fall.
- **Mend.** The angel carries a store of healing (its Mend action), and it departs when that store is spent.
- **Bear.** Name a creature you know or a place you have seen within 1 mile of you. The angel takes a spoken message, or an object weighing up to 10 pounds, and goes by the ladder: it vanishes, arrives there within the minute, delivers it, and departs.

The angel shares your Initiative and takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your commands (no action required) about where it moves and whom its errand serves; with no command, it pursues its errand on its own. It departs when its errand ends, when it drops to 0 Hit Points, when you dismiss it (no action required), or after 1 minute.

You run the angel in a fight. Out of one, the DM speaks for it, and it remembers you.

Calling an angel counts as expending a spell slot to cast a spell for the rule that you can expend only one spell slot on a turn: you can't call an angel and cast a spell with a spell slot on the same turn. You can have only one angel at a time, and one in each fight: once you've called an angel, you can't call another until you next roll Initiative or finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Tongue of Fire
features.text: You can speak, read, and write Celestial. In addition, you know the names, seals, and ranks of the messengers as your tradition records them, and you have Advantage on Intelligence (Religion) checks about angels, Celestials, and the heavens.

features.name: Chain and Tome
features.text: If you have the Pact of the Chain invocation, your familiar can't take a Fiend or Undead form, and it can take the form of a cherub (stat block below).

features.name: Messenger
features.text:
You always have *Sending* prepared. Once per Long Rest, you can cast it without a spell slot, and an angel bears the message.

**Letters of Credence.** You were made to carry messages, and courts can tell. You know the protocol of any court or household you enter: precedence, titles, forms of address, which door to use and when to kneel. In addition, anyone who reads a letter you wrote and signed knows whether you believed it when you wrote it.

features.name: Greater Angels
features.text:
Your angels are greater angels: use the Angel table's level 10 row. In addition, when the creature a Strike angel is attacking drops to 0 Hit Points, you can name another (no action required); the angel still departs at the end of its second turn. An angel whose only errand is Guard has Resistance to all damage.

**Stranger at the Door.** The oldest hospitality stories are about angels at the door. Households that keep the old laws of hospitality (most of them, across the Abrahamic world and well beyond) give you food and a bed for a night without asking payment. When you accept a host's food or bed, you can ask the DM whether your host means you harm under their roof, and the DM answers truly.

features.name: Archangel
features.text:
When you call an angel, you can call an archangel instead (the Angel table's archangel row). It takes both the Strike and Guard errands at once (name a creature for each when you call it), departing only when it drops to 0 Hit Points or after 1 minute. It uses Multiattack as a Strike angel and Intercede as a Guard angel. When its Strike target drops, you name a new one (no action required).

When it arrives, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Prone condition and be Frightened of the archangel until the end of that creature's next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**Visitation.** Once every 7 days, you can call your archangel for a visitation, not a fight: it appears for 1 minute, takes no errand, and harms no one, and every creature within 1 mile that can see it knows a messenger of the highest rank has come. Crowds kneel, riots stop, and a wedding or a funeral is remembered for a hundred years. A visitation costs no spell slot and doesn't use your Archangel.

**Call on the Ladder.** You can call on the ladder the angels climb between the heavens and the world. Once per Long Rest, you can cast *Plane Shift* without a spell slot or Material components, with these changes: it affects only you and willing creatures, and you arrive where you choose within 1 mile of a place you have seen on that plane.

> **Playing an Envoy**
>
> Every fight asks one question: which errand? Strike, and the angel goes for the creature you name with a blade of light; Guard, and it stands at the shoulder of the daring one, the one about to jump, and catches them if they fall; Mend, and it walks the field laying hands on your friends. Whatever its errand, an angel on the field is something your enemies have to deal with. The angel's turn follows its errand, so your turn stays quick: call, blast, and watch it work. Between fights, the angel is a courier who remembers you, and the DM speaks for it.

data.name: Geomancer
data.lead:
*The Geometry Underneath Everything Is Yours*

> **The Geomancer at a Glance**
>
> **Figures** are your craft. As a Bonus Action, you draw a Figure on a surface within 60 feet: Intelligence modifier uses, back on a Short or Long Rest. Each Figure is a fixed shape with fixed numbers, and it affects only the creatures you choose.
>
> | Figure | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | Square | one creature falls 10 feet sideways and has the Prone condition; or a friend walks on walls for a minute | Level 3 |
> | Circle | one creature can't leave; a Square inside it holds it down (and from 10th, for two more uses, it can't move or act on its next turn) | Level 6 |
> | Vesica Piscis | a slow hour, and a quick one (two uses) | Level 10 |
> | Nested Spheres | a second turn, once per Long Rest | Level 14 |
>
> **What it looks like:** a spell leaves your hands while your foot draws a Figure in the dust: the Square under the archer on the wall, who goes sideways off it (a Strength save), or the Circle around the brute coming for you, who finds he can't step out (a Wisdom save).

features.name: Geomancer Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Wizard level specified in the Geomancer Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared, and they are in your spellbook. They don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

| Wizard Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Feather Fall*, *Levitate* |
| 5 | *Haste*, *Slow* |
| 7 | *Dimension Door*, *Resilient Sphere* |
| 9 | *Hold Monster*, *Telekinesis* |

features.name: The Plumb Line
features.text: You always know which way is down, how high you are above or below the ground or the sea, and the hour to the minute. By holding an object for a moment, you know its weight to the ounce.

features.name: Shop Talk
features.text: You gain proficiency with one of the following tools of your choice: Cartographer's Tools, Mason's Tools, or Navigator's Tools. In addition, masons, surveyors, instrument-makers, tilers, and astronomers anywhere in the world recognize you as one of theirs: given an hour among them, you can find a bed, a meal, a bench to borrow, and the local gossip about whatever's being built. You also know the sixteen figures of sand divination well enough to cast a chart for a paying client. It has no magical effect.

features.name: Figures
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you inscribe a Figure you know on a surface you can see within 60 feet of yourself: a floor, a wall, a ceiling, or the ground. You can inscribe Figures a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

A Figure is a ruled line of light, visible to anyone who can see its surface, and it is magical. It affects only the creatures you choose when you inscribe it, and it does exactly what its rule says: its distances are fixed and its damage isn't rolled. Most Figures act once and fade; a Circle stays, and you can have only one Circle at a time. When a Figure calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

You know the Square. You learn the Circle at Wizard level 6 and the Vesica Piscis at Wizard level 10.

**Square**
-
- You inscribe the Square on the surface under one creature you can see that is on that surface, filling its space. When you inscribe it, name one of the Square's edges as down.
- An unwilling creature makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it falls up to 10 feet toward that edge. This is forced movement, and it stops early if the creature meets another creature or a solid surface. The creature then has the Prone condition and takes Bludgeoning damage equal to your Intelligence modifier. If it ends this movement with nothing to support it, it then falls normally.
- A willing creature doesn't fall. Instead, for 1 minute, it can walk on walls and ceilings as if they were floors. If the minute ends while it's on a wall or a ceiling, it falls.

features.name: The Compass Circle
features.text:
You learn another Figure:

**Circle**
-
- You inscribe the Circle around the space of one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The Circle's space extends 10 feet up from the surface. It lasts for 1 minute, until the creature leaves it, or until you inscribe another Circle.
- When the creature tries to leave the Circle's space by its own movement, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is back in the space it left, the movement it spent is lost, and it can't try to leave again until its next turn. On a successful save, it leaves, and the Circle fades.
- If the creature teleports or another effect moves it out of the Circle, the Circle fades.
- A creature inside your Circle that fails its saving throw against your Square doesn't fall: it has the Prone condition and takes the damage where it stands, and the Circle doesn't fade.

**Squaring the Map.** Given an hour at a vantage point, you can draw an accurate map of everything you can see, its distances true to within a yard in a hundred. By the sun or the stars you can find your latitude, and with a clock you trust, your longitude, which the navies of Europe still can't do. In addition, after 10 minutes of pacing a building, you know whether its inside and outside measurements disagree, and roughly where: a hollow wall, a sealed room, a stair that isn't on the plan.

features.name: The Vesica Piscis
features.text:
You learn another Figure:

**Vesica Piscis**
-
- Inscribing the Vesica Piscis expends two uses of your Figures.
- The Figure fills a 15-foot Cube that rests on the inscribed surface. Each creature you choose in it is caught in one of its two hours, your choice for each:
    - *The slow hour.* The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, until the start of your next turn, its Speed is halved, it can't take Reactions, and on its turn it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both.
    - *The quick hour.* A willing creature can immediately move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

**Figure Within Figure.** When you inscribe your Square on a creature inside your Circle, you can expend two more uses of your Figures to draw the one figure inside the other. If you do and the creature fails its saving throw, the Circle holds it harder: as well as the Prone condition and the damage, it has the Incapacitated condition and its Speed is 0 until the start of your next turn.

**Ephemeris.** With a day's work and paper, you can compute the sky for any date and place: eclipses, the moon's phase, sunrise and sunset, the tides at a known port, the auspicious and inauspicious hours by any court's reckoning, and the length of a shadow at noon. In a contest of calendars, you're right to the minute.

features.name: The Nested Spheres
features.text:
At the start of your turn (no action required), you can stand inside the Nested Spheres. When this turn ends, you take another turn immediately. During the second turn, you can't expend a spell slot. Other creatures can take Reactions normally during both turns. An effect that lasts until the start or the end of your turn counts each of the two turns. The Figure fades when the second turn ends.

Using this feature doesn't expend a use of your Figures. Once you use it, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**Wrong Angles.** You can see where the world's geometry has been bent. When you enter a place, or as a Bonus Action, you can ask the DM whether any place within 60 feet of you is thin ground (*Life on the Border*), and whether magic has altered the shape of a place you can see within the last day: a Figure, a Danae's warp, a teleportation circle, a passage opened through a wall. The DM answers truly.

> **Playing a Geomancer**
>
> Put your Figures on the map: a square of string or a card for the Square, a ring for the Circle. A Figure holds only what it was drawn for: even the Circle, which lasts a minute, holds only the one creature it was drawn around.
>
> - **Down until its turn.** A creature you Square stays on the ground until it stands up on its own turn, so it lies there while your friends act; Prone gives Disadvantage to ranged attacks against it, yours included.
> - **Circle, then Square.** From 6th level, a Square inside your Circle pins the creature where it stands; from 10th, with two more uses, it can't move or act on its next turn either: most of your Figures until you rest, drawn around one creature.
> - **The willing Square is a gift.** One Bonus Action sends your rogue up the palazzo wall and across the roofs for a minute.
> - **The Nested Spheres.** A second turn while the world waits: time to draw the Circle and then the Square before the creature can walk out, to work a spell like *Telekinesis* twice, or to cross a room twice.

data.name: Path of the Bordermarch
data.lead:
*Ride Out with the Hunt*

> **The Bordermarch at a Glance**
>
> **Your Rage is the ríastrad.** When you Rage, your body turns in its skin: your reach grows, light rises from your brow, you gain Temporary Hit Points, and you can push through the ranks of anyone you've hit.
>
> **Going deeper is a choice.** Once per Short or Long Rest, you can let the ríastrad take you deeper. Your hits deal more damage, but you can't tell friend from foe. You can't end it yourself: it ends when your Rage does, a turn after the last enemy near you falls, or when you're cooled (a bucket of water thrown over you, *Create or Destroy Water*, a plunge into cold water, or Cold damage from anyone, foes included). If it ends any way but cooling, it costs you a level of Exhaustion until you rest.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | The Ríastrad | Rage: +5 feet of reach, light, Temporary Hit Points; move through creatures you've hit | Level 3 |
> | The Deep Ríastrad | +1d6 Force on each hit; Friend or Foe; ends with your Rage, the fight's end, or cooling; 1 Exhaustion until you rest unless you were cooled | Level 6 |
> | Strike and Vanish | after a hit, teleport 10 feet | Level 10 |
> | The Hunt Rides | going deep frightens your enemies; while deep, you're Large and make one more attack | Level 14 |
>
> **What it looks like:** the light stands up from your brow, and you push through the first defender to reach the one behind. When you go deep, your friends are already a step out of your reach, because they've seen it before. When it's over, the water bearer walks in with the bucket, and you come back to yourself with nothing to pay.

**A Hidden Creature.** A Bordermarch Barbarian is a Hidden creature ("The Hidden, in the rules," in this book's introduction): iron and salt bind it, and someone has to ask it in.

features.name: The Ríastrad
features.text:
While your Rage is active, you gain the following benefits:

- **Twisted.** Your reach increases by 5 feet.
- **The Hero's Light.** Light rises from your brow, shedding Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. You can't take the Hide action.
- **Through the Ranks.** You can move through the space of any creature you've hit with a melee attack this turn. You can't end your move in its space.

When you enter your Rage, you also gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Barbarian level (round down).

features.name: Of the Border
features.text: The tide runs in your blood. You always know whether the Hidden are at the flood or the ebb where you are, and how many nights remain until the next open night. You also know the direction of the nearest thin ground within 1 mile, and you can't become lost by nonmagical means. Wherever the border's old customs hold, a household that asks you in gives you a guest's seat at its fire until dawn, and border people tell a guest what they wouldn't tell a stranger at the door.

features.name: The Deep Ríastrad
features.text:
When you enter your Rage, or as a Bonus Action while your Rage is active, you can let the ríastrad take you deeper. The Deep Ríastrad lasts until your Rage ends, you're cooled (see below), or The Fight's End ends it, and you can't end either one yourself. While it lasts, your Rage stays active without your extending it, and it doesn't end early unless you have the Incapacitated condition. The following also apply:

- **Ríastrad Strikes.** Each time you hit a creature with an attack using a melee weapon, it takes an extra 1d6 Force damage.
- **Friend or Foe.** You can't tell them apart. At the start of each of your turns, note the creature nearest to you that you can see (if several are equally near, you choose one). If that creature is within your reach, your first attack roll this turn must target it, whoever it is.
- **Engaging Distraction.** When you make an attack roll against an ally, any ally within 30 feet of you that you can see can take a Reaction to catch your eye. The attack roll has Disadvantage.
- **The Fight's End.** If no enemy remains within 60 feet of you that you can see, the Deep Ríastrad ends at the end of your next turn.

**Cooling the Hero.** Cold water in sizable amounts, or cold itself, cools you. When you're cooled, the Deep Ríastrad ends; your Rage doesn't. You're cooled when any of the following happens:

- **Water.** Cold water drenches you: another creature within 5 feet of you takes the Utilize action to throw at least a full bucket of water over you on purpose; *Create or Destroy Water* is cast so that the water falls on you; or you're plunged into, or fall into, cold water deep enough to go under. A splash, a waterskin, or rain doesn't cool you.
- **Cold.** You take Cold damage from any creature or effect, an enemy's included. You can choose to fail a saving throw against an effect that would deal you Cold damage, but the effect must deal you at least 1 Cold damage to cool you.

You can't cool yourself: water you enter on purpose doesn't count.

When the Deep Ríastrad ends, you gain 1 Exhaustion level, unless it ended because you were cooled. Track this Exhaustion apart from Exhaustion from other sources; you lose it when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Strike and Vanish
features.text: Once on each of your turns, immediately after you hit a creature with a melee attack while your Rage is active, you can step through the Hidden: you teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

features.name: The Hunt Rides
features.text:
While your Deep Ríastrad lasts, you gain the following benefits:

- **The Full Ríastrad.** You can make one extra attack when you take the Attack action. Your size also becomes Large, if you're smaller and there is room; if there isn't room, you become as large as the space allows. Your reach doesn't change from this. If an effect such as *Enlarge/Reduce* increases your size while you're Large, it makes you Huge.
- **The Hunt.** When you enter the Deep Ríastrad, each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can see you makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, it has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. A Frightened creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

> **Playing a Bordermarch Barbarian**
>
> You ride the ríastrad; the Deep Ríastrad rides you. You go deep once a rest. Tell the table before the fight, so the Rogue can fight from outside your 10-foot reach; nobody wants to learn that mid-swing.
>
> Friend or Foe is about positions. If an enemy is as near to you as any ally, you choose the enemy. Your reach grows when you Rage, and your friends learn to stand a step farther off. Through the Ranks lets you push past the one you hit to the one behind, and at 10th level Strike and Vanish lets you put yourself among enemies after each hit.
>
> Someone has to be the water bearer. When the last enemy falls, the Deep Ríastrad runs one more turn: if anyone is within your reach then, your first swing goes to them. The party can wait it out at a distance, but then you pay the Exhaustion. Cool you instead (a full bucket from someone within 5 feet, *Create or Destroy Water*, or a *Ray of Frost* from across the field) and you pay nothing. A party with no caster can manage with a bucket, but someone has to carry it and keep it full (*Euphonia: The Setting* has the Water-Bearer's Bucket, in Characters, Wonders and Curiosities). Cooling you in the middle of a fight works too: it ends the Deep Ríastrad early and spares you the Exhaustion. So does an enemy that deals Cold damage: against a white dragon or a winter wolf, the Deep Ríastrad won't last, but it won't cost you either.
>
> When you do swing at an ally, the ally who catches your eye (Engaging Distraction) doesn't have to be the one you're swinging at.
>
> At 14th level the Full Ríastrad makes you Large: you take up a 10-foot square, you can grapple Huge creatures, and you have to squeeze down a corridor a Medium hero walks.

data.name: Path of the Faebreaker
data.lead:
*Hold On and Don't Let Go*

> **The Faebreaker at a Glance**
>
> **Your Rage is a grip.** While you Rage, you can grab whatever you hit without letting go of your weapon. Whatever you hold can't get free easily, can't fight well, can't teleport or change its shape to get away, and it hurts.
>
> **Friend or foe: you hold one.** Your grip is on an enemy or on a friend, never both. Take hold of a friend when something comes to carry them off, or when they need you to shield them: a friend you hold has Half Cover, and from 6th level you can bear what's hitting them.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | Hold Fast | while raging: grab on a hit, no free hand needed; what you hold has Disadvantage on attacks and escape, can't teleport or change shape to get free, and takes damage at the start of each of your turns | Level 3 |
> | Hold a Friend | take hold of an ally instead: it has Half Cover, and nothing moves, teleports, or carries it off without you | Level 3 |
> | By Touch | what you hold, you know: whether it's Hidden, whether its shape is its own | Level 3 |
> | Bear the Burning | take the hits meant for the friend you hold | Level 6 |
> | The Night Turns | hold one of the taken from dusk to dawn and win them back | Level 6 |
> | Pull Them Back | a Reaction to rush to an ally who falls, is taken, or is grabbed, and take hold of them | Level 10 |
> | Through Every Shape | what you hold is Restrained; a friend you hold shakes off charms and changes; Temporary Hit Points when you Rage | Level 14 |
>
> **What it looks like:** the rider you hit is still in your arms when the next one comes, and it can't flicker away or change its shape to get free. When the Mortal Hunter turns to your friend, you let go and take hold of them, and nothing carries them off while you have them.

**Not a Hidden Creature.** A Faebreaker has nothing of the Hidden in it, which is why its grip holds.

features.name: Hold Fast
features.text:
While your Rage is active, you gain the following benefits:

- **Reality's Grip.** You can Grapple a creature without a free hand: you hold it with your arm, your knees, and your weight, and your hands stay on your weapon. You can hold only one creature at a time this way (see Hold a Friend). When your Rage ends, a creature you hold this way is released unless you have a hand free to keep the grapple.
- **Take Hold.** Once on each of your turns, immediately after you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can try to Grapple it (as the Grapple option of your Unarmed Strike) without using an attack.
- **It Can't Get Away.** The creature you have Grappled has Disadvantage on attack rolls, including against you, and on ability checks to escape your grapple. It can't teleport, and changing its shape or size doesn't free it, whatever size it becomes. If it has the Invisible condition, it gains no benefit from it against you, and you always know where it is.
- **The Grip Bites.** At the start of each of your turns, the creature you have Grappled takes Force damage equal to a roll of d6s, one for each point of your Rage Damage bonus.

**Nothing Takes What You Hold.** A creature you hold, by Hold Fast or Hold a Friend, can't be Taken unless the taker beats you in the contest (Taken, in "The Hidden, in the rules").

features.name: Hold a Friend
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can take hold of a willing creature within 5 feet of yourself; this counts as your one hold under Hold Fast, so you let go of anything else you hold (outside your Rage, it takes a free hand). The creature doesn't have the Grappled condition: it moves with you when you move (at half your Speed unless it is Tiny or two sizes smaller than you), and the hold ends if it moves away from you, you let go (no action required), or you have the Incapacitated condition.

While you hold it, the creature has Half Cover, and it can't be moved, teleported, or carried away against its will unless you go with it. It has Advantage on saving throws against effects that would move it, teleport it, or change its shape against its will.

features.name: By Touch
features.text: While you hold a creature, by Hold Fast or Hold a Friend, you know whether it is a Hidden creature, and whether an illusion or a shape-changing effect is disguising it (though not what its true form is). You also recognize any creature you know well while you touch it, whatever shape or glamour it wears.

features.name: Bear the Burning
features.text: When a creature you hold by Hold a Friend takes damage from an attack or an effect, you can take a Reaction to take that damage instead of it. Your own Resistances and Immunities apply to the damage you take; any other effect of the attack or effect (a condition, a push) still falls on the creature you hold.

features.name: The Night Turns
features.text:
You can win back a creature the Hidden have taken or swapped: a stolen child, a bride carried off, a rider of the Hunt who was once a villager, a creature left in someone's place. You must hold it from dusk to dawn, without letting go, through every shape it is forced into: by Hold Fast, by Hold a Friend, or by an ordinary Grapple. For The Night Turns, a grip begun by Hold Fast doesn't end when your Rage does and still needs no free hand. You don't need to be raging, and it needn't be willing: through The Night Turns, the creature can't escape your grip by any means. If you let go, or have the Incapacitated condition, the night is lost and you must begin again on another night.

At dawn, the creature is won back: the taking or the swap is broken; any charm, curse, or shape-change the Hidden laid on it ends; and a creature left in its place goes back to the Hidden. The DM says what a creature has been taken by, and what it is like when it comes back. By default it was taken by the Hunt, and it comes back with one thing from the Hidden: a tune, a habit, or a debt (Running the Hunt, After the Night).

> **Running The Night Turns**
>
> The night is a scene with several rolls. Pick three or more shapes for the Hidden to force on the creature, one an hour or at the moments the story wants, and let each one test the holder once. The DC is 13, or 15 for a great power of the Hidden (a lord or lady of a court). Allies can't take the burden, but they can heal the holder, keep the fire lit, and keep whatever comes to interrupt away.
>
> | Shape | What it does to the one holding it |
> |---|---|
> | An adder, or a snake | It bites: Constitution saving throw, or the Poisoned condition until dawn. |
> | A bear, a lion, or a wolf | It mauls: 2d8 Slashing damage, or half as much on a successful Strength saving throw. |
> | A bar of red-hot iron, or a burning coal | It burns: 3d6 Fire damage, or half as much on a successful Constitution saving throw. |
> | An eel, or a rope of running water | It slips: Strength (Athletics) check, or Disadvantage on your next saving throw this night. |
> | Something pitiable: a weeping child, your own mother dying | It begs: Wisdom saving throw, or the Frightened condition until the next shape. You can hold on while Frightened. |
>
> The last shape is always its own: the night is done, and it's only a person again.

features.name: Pull Them Back
features.text: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself drops to 0 Hit Points, is about to be moved, teleported, carried away, or Taken against its will, or is Grappled or Restrained by another creature, you can take a Reaction to go to it. You move up to your Speed toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks; if you end within 5 feet of it, you take hold of it as if by Hold a Friend (it must be willing, or have the Unconscious condition). If you take hold of it, it isn't moved, teleported, or carried away by that effect, and the other creature's grapple or restraint on it ends; if it was about to be Taken, you hold on instead, with the contest in Taken. If you reach it but can't take hold, none of this happens.

features.name: Through Every Shape
features.text:
While your Rage is active, you gain the following benefits:

- **Held Fast.** The creature you have Grappled by Hold Fast also has the Restrained condition.
- **Won Back.** At the end of each of your turns, a creature you hold by Hold a Friend can end one of the following effects on itself: the Charmed condition, the Frightened condition, or an effect that changed its shape against its will.
- **Steeled.** When you enter your Rage, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier plus half your Barbarian level (round down).

> **Playing a Faebreaker Barbarian**
>
> The grip is a choice of who: the rider you won't let ride away, the thing that came for your friend. Whatever you hold stays held while the fight goes on around it. The grip works on anything, Hidden or not.
>
> Let go when a friend needs you: a friend you hold has Half Cover, nothing takes them while you hold on, and from 6th level you can take the blows meant for them. Bearing the burning has a price you can see: if you fall, nobody is holding on.
>
> Holding is your motion. What you hold moves when you do (at half your Speed): drag a rider off its horse, haul the Bard out of its own song, carry the thing across the ford, or into the Killer's ward where it can't vanish.

data.name: Hidden Bard
data.lead:
*Remember What You Never Learned*

> **The Hidden Bard at a Glance**
>
> **Remembering** is what you carry. You remember a skill, a tongue, a piece of lore, a song, or (from level 6) a spell you never learned. Each one goes on your **tally**, and the Hidden is owed: you **sing your case**, a Charisma (Performance) check against DC 6 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus twice your tally. Succeed, and you owe nothing. Fail, and the Hidden takes its due: your voice for a turn, a level of Exhaustion, or (once per Long Rest) a tongue that can't lie.
>
> **Sing the Season** is your Bonus Action. Spend Bardic Inspiration (or remember the song, and owe for it) to sing spring, summer, autumn, or winter into a person. From level 6 you can sing it into a place, and the music carries where it carries: a place takes everyone in it, friend or foe.
>
> **Read the Room** tells you the tempers in a fight, one for each group of like creatures. A season that **matches** a creature's temper lands hard (Disadvantage on the save, and a stronger effect); the **opposite** season slides off (Advantage on the save).
>
> | Season | Save | Fails | Matched |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Spring | Strength | pushed 15 feet | and Prone |
> | Summer | Dexterity | 2 Bardic Inspiration dice of Fire (half on a success) | 4 dice |
> | Autumn | Wisdom | Charmed, or Disadvantage on its next save | both |
> | Winter | Constitution | Speed 0 | and no Reactions, and an action or a Bonus Action, not both |
>
> **What it looks like:** the fight opens, and you already know who in it is afraid and who is furious. You sing winter to the frightened one and it stops where it stands; the furious one hears summer, and the song catches fire around it. When the Hidden asks for its due, you sing your case, and the room listens.

**A Hidden Creature.** A Hidden Bard is a Hidden creature ("The Hidden, in the rules," in this book's introduction), and the Hidden in it is what remembers. The Hunt's fiddlers and remembrancers are Hidden Bards.

features.name: A Piece of the Hidden
features.text:
You gain the following benefits.

**Tongue.** You know Sylvan.

**Read the Room.** As a Bonus Action, or as part of rolling Initiative, you read the room: the DM tells you the **temper** of the creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself, one for each group of like creatures and one for any creature that stands apart. You can also read the room without an action by watching for 1 minute. Reading the room tells you tempers; it doesn't make a creature *read*, which only the Danae's Reading the Season does. A temper is always one of the four seasons:

| Temper | What lies under it |
|---|---|
| Spring | hope, curiosity, a beginning |
| Summer | passion, anger, confidence |
| Autumn | longing, regret, decline |
| Winter | fear, grief, resolve |

Spring and autumn are **opposites**, and so are summer and winter. The DM assigns tempers, and says how long one holds (Tempers, in "The Hidden, in the rules"). Once you've read the room, you keep the list: note each temper the DM tells you, and each one you turn. While you know a creature's temper, you have Advantage on Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion) checks against it that play to that temper.

features.name: Remembering
features.text:
You can **remember** any of the following. Each time you do, it goes on your **tally**, and you owe the Hidden a **Due**, which you settle at once (see "The Hidden's Due," below). You can't remember while the Hidden has your voice.

- **A Skill.** When you make an ability check with a skill or tool, before you roll, you remember it: you have proficiency and Expertise in it for that check. You can't remember Performance.
- **A Tongue.** As a Bonus Action, you remember a language you have heard spoken or seen written. For 1 hour, you can speak, read, and write it.
- **A Lore.** As a Magic action, you name a creature, place, or object you can see or are holding, and ask one question about it. The DM answers truthfully, in a sentence, with what the Hidden remembers of it: old things, the dead, the fae, oaths, curses, and the ways in and out of places, not the plans of the living.
- **A Song.** When you Sing the Season, you can remember the song instead of expending Bardic Inspiration.

> **The Hidden's Due**
>
> When you remember, first add it to your **tally**: a skill, a tongue, a lore, or a song counts as one; a spell counts as one plus its level. Your tally goes back to 0 when you finish a Long Rest.
>
> What you remember happens first (the skill applies to that check, the song or spell takes effect). Then you settle: sing your case to the Hidden by making a Charisma (Performance) check. The DC is 6 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus twice your tally, whether you paid for the earlier ones or not. On a success, the Hidden is satisfied, and you owe nothing.
>
> On a failure, the Hidden takes its due. Choose one:
>
> - **The Hidden Keeps Your Voice.** You can't speak or sing: you can't cast spells that have a Verbal component, sing a season, or remember. In combat, this lasts until the end of your next turn. Out of combat, the Hidden keeps your voice until you finish a Short or Long Rest. A spell you're already concentrating on continues.
> - **Seven Years in a Night.** You gain one level of Exhaustion.
> - **A Tongue That Cannot Lie.** Until you finish a Long Rest, you can't knowingly speak a falsehood. Once you choose this price, you can't choose it again until you finish a Long Rest.
>
> The DM can let the Hidden name a different price of the same weight, one that fits the story: a promise, a gift left at a hawthorn, a dance at the next full moon.

features.name: Sing the Season
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to sing a season (spring, summer, autumn, or winter) into a person: one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that can hear you is subject to the season. Instead of expending Bardic Inspiration, you can remember the song (see Remembering).

A creature subject to a season makes the saving throw the season calls for against your spell save DC. A creature whose temper **matches** the season has Disadvantage on the save, and if it fails, it also suffers the season's matched effect. A creature whose temper is the season's **opposite** has Advantage on the save. A creature's temper counts whether or not you've read it.

| Season | Effect | Matched |
|---|---|---|
| **Spring** | *Strength saving throw.* On a failed save, you push the creature up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice. A willing creature can instead teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. | It also has the Prone condition. |
| **Summer** | *Dexterity saving throw.* Roll two of your Bardic Inspiration dice. The creature takes that much Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. | Roll four dice instead of two. |
| **Autumn** | *Wisdom saving throw.* On a failed save, choose one: the creature has the Charmed condition, with you as the charmer, until the end of its next turn, or it has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn. | Both. |
| **Winter** | *Constitution saving throw.* On a failed save, the creature's Speed is 0 until the end of its next turn. | Until the end of its next turn, it also can't take Reactions, and on its turn it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both. |

features.name: Remember a Spell
features.text: When you would cast a spell, you can instead cast one you don't have prepared, as long as it's on the Bard, Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list and is a cantrip or of a level for which you have spell slots. You cast it normally, expending a spell slot if it needs one, and you remember it: it counts as one plus its level in your tally (the slot's level, if you expend a higher one; a cantrip counts as one). The spell counts as a Bard spell for you.

features.name: Into a Place
features.text: When you Sing the Season, you can sing it into a place instead of a person. Expend one use of Bardic Inspiration, or remember the song. Choose a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Every creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered there that can hear you is subject to the season, whether you want it to be or not.

features.name: The Teind
features.text: When you owe the Hidden a Due, you can choose not to sing your case, and sing the teind onto another instead; you can also do so when the Hidden would take its due from you after a failed check. Choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that can hear you. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it pays instead of you: it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, and you pay nothing. On a successful save, you pay as usual. You can sing the teind onto another twice, and you regain both uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Turn the Season
features.text:
When a creature fails its saving throw against a season you sing, its temper turns to that season for 1 hour, and its mood follows: hope, anger, longing, or fear. It doesn't know you did it unless it sees you sing and understands what you are.

> **Playing a Hidden Bard**
>
> Keep your tally where you can see it: the Due's DC is 6 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus twice the tally. Every Due is a performance, sung to something old and listening, and your Performance is how you argue your case. In a fight the Hidden takes your voice for a turn, not the fight, and it takes it after the song or spell has done its work. A remembered spell weighs one plus its level, so a *Fireball* remembered late in the day is a gamble the whole table can feel. From 14th, twice a day, the Teind lets you skip the argument and send the bill to an enemy instead.
>
> Remember what nobody at the table can do: the tongue nobody speaks, the lock nobody can pick, the old story nobody knows. A skill your friend already has is their moment, not yours.
>
> Your song lands once, and from 6th it can take everyone in the room.

data.name: Hidden Domain
data.lead:
> **The Hidden Domain at a Glance**
>
> **Strike a Bargain** is your Channel Divinity. As a Magic action, you ask the Hidden for one of two things. The **tide** decides which goes better, and you always know it.
>
> | Ask | What it does | At its tide |
> |---|---|---|
> | Turn Aside | creatures you choose within 30 feet make a Wisdom saving throw or are Incapacitated until your next turn | at the flood, they have Disadvantage on the save |
> | Bring Back | creatures you choose within 30 feet at 0 Hit Points, Charmed, Frightened, or Taken (unless Taken on thin ground) get back up | at the ebb, double the Hit Points, and it reaches the Bloodied too |
>
> **Rowan and Red Thread** (level 6): one ward at a time, tied on a rest. Advantage against Charmed and Frightened, and it turns one drop to 0 Hit Points into 1.
>
> **Not Dead, Only Away** (level 17): Bring Back reaches a creature that died in the last minute, and you can ward a village's heart against the Hidden for a night.
>
> **What it looks like:** at the flood, the riders come over the green and the Hidden lead them astray, and they stand blinking in the wrong field while the village gets its doors shut. At the ebb, two of your friends are down or glamoured, and you call them both back at once.

**Not a Hidden Creature.** A Cleric of the Hidden Domain speaks for its people to the Hidden, and carries nothing of it.

features.name: Hidden Domain Spells
features.text:
Your connection to the hill ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Hidden Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Cleric Level | Prepared Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Calm Emotions*, *Charm Person*, *Lesser Restoration*, *Protection from Evil and Good* |
| 5 | *Magic Circle*, *Remove Curse* |
| 7 | *Banishment*, *Locate Creature* |
| 9 | *Dispel Evil and Good*, *Geas* |

features.name: The Go-Between
features.text:
You gain the following benefits.

**The Tide.** You always know the tide where you are (see "The Tide," below), and you know whether a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is a Hidden creature.

**Tongue.** You know Sylvan, the Hidden's speech, as your own people hear it and name it.

**Parley.** Before Initiative is rolled, you can call out to Hidden creatures that can hear you and offer parley under the old courtesies: iron put away, a gift held out, no names given. They hear you out, in Sylvan or any language you share, unless they have a reason not to (the DM decides; by default they hear you, because the old courtesies are strong, and a reason is something like a bargain broken or a debt the village owes them). For up to 1 minute, while you talk, they don't attack you or anyone you speak for. The parley ends if you or anyone you speak for attacks, casts a spell, or draws iron. Once a parley ends in a fight, you can't offer parley to those creatures again until you finish a Long Rest.

**Bargains.** You have Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks to read a Hidden creature, and on Charisma (Persuasion) checks to strike a bargain with one, and you can use your Wisdom modifier for those Persuasion checks. A bargain you strike with the Hidden binds both sides (see "Bargains with the Hidden," below).

> **The Tide**
>
> The tide, the raiding season, and the open nights are in "The Hidden, in the rules" in this book's introduction. On the open nights the tide is whichever you need for each use of Strike a Bargain and each bargain you make under Bargains with the Hidden. A place of power can keep its own tide: under the fairy hill itself, it might always be at the flood.

features.name: Strike a Bargain
features.text:
As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to strike a bargain with the Hidden, choosing one of the following asks.

**Turn Aside.** Each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of yourself makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. At the flood, it has Disadvantage on the save. On a failed save, the Hidden lead it astray: it has the Incapacitated condition until the start of your next turn. A Hidden creature that has broken a bargain struck through you fails this save automatically.

**Bring Back.** Choose any number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself that have 0 Hit Points and aren't dead, or that have the Charmed or Frightened condition. Each of them regains Hit Points equal to your Cleric level plus your Wisdom modifier, and its Charmed and Frightened conditions end. At the ebb, the Hit Points are doubled, and you can also choose creatures that are Bloodied.

You can also call back any creature that was Taken from a place within 30 feet of you, whatever took it, unless it was Taken on thin ground: it is no longer Taken, reappears in the space it left or the nearest unoccupied space, and regains Hit Points as above.

> **Bargains with the Hidden**
>
> Out of a fight, the go-between's work is talk. To ask the Hidden for something on someone's behalf, find them (at a hill, a ring, a hawthorn, a crossroads at the right hour, or your people's equivalent), offer parley, and ask for one thing: give back someone who is away, lift what afflicts the fairy-struck (a person, a cow, the butter that won't come), turn a raid aside, or settle what's owed.
>
> **The price.** The DM names a price: a gift, a service, a promise, or something dear. The tide sets how steep it is. At the flood, asking them to go is fair, and asking for something back is dear; at the ebb, the reverse. Pay it, and it's done, to the letter.
>
> **What's owed.** If either side breaks a bargain, the other is owed. When the Hidden owe you or the people you speak for, you can call the debt in once: the creature that owes must do one thing you ask of it that the DM agrees is in its power and doesn't cost its life. Until it pays, it fails its saves against your Turn Aside.

features.name: Rowan and Red Thread
features.text:
When you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can tie a ward on one creature you touch. You can have only one ward tied at a time; tying another unties the first. While a creature wears your ward, it has Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

When the warded creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points and isn't killed outright, the ward breaks, and the creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead.

features.name: Not Dead, Only Away
features.text:
**The Newly Dead.** When you use Bring Back, you can also choose a creature that died within the last minute and whose body is within 30 feet of yourself. It returns to life with 0 Hit Points and then regains Hit Points as Bring Back says. This can't return a creature that died of old age, and it doesn't restore missing body parts.

**Ward the Village.** You can cast *Hallow* without expending a spell slot or material components, and the casting takes you 1 hour. Cast this way, the spell keeps out Hidden creatures other than those you choose when you cast it, whatever their creature type, along with any types you choose for it; its area can be any part of a settlement up to 300 feet on a side; and it lasts until the next dawn. Once you cast it this way, you can't cast it this way again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Hidden Domain Cleric**
>
> You always know the tide, and the tide tells you what the Hidden will do for you. At the flood, when the Hunt rides hardest, they'll gladly lead the riders astray: the riders save against Turn Aside at Disadvantage, and every one it catches loses its actions, Bonus Actions and Reactions until your next turn. At the ebb, they can't keep hold of what they took: Bring Back reaches every one of you who is down, Charmed, Frightened, or Taken, at double the Hit Points.
>
