> Talk first. Parley comes before Initiative, so offer it before anyone draws iron: a minute of talk is a minute nobody is hitting you, and a bargain struck there binds both sides. A Hidden creature that breaks one fails its saves against your Turn Aside until it pays.
>
> Rowan and Red Thread goes on whoever the Hunt will come for first: the child, the bride, the new mother. Thin ground belongs to the Hidden, and Bring Back can't reach a friend Taken there.

data.name: Hidden Killer
data.lead:
> **The Hidden Killer at a Glance**
>
> **Before the fight:** Read the Tide to learn whether the Hidden are abroad, and which way. Then Prepare the Ground: ward the place they'll come to. A fight on your ground starts on your terms. Caught off it, throw the ward down where you stand.
>
> **In the fight:** Cold Iron is extra damage once a turn against anything, and more against the Hidden. Your *Hunter's Mark* sees through what the Hidden hide behind.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | Read the Tide | know whether the Hidden are abroad, and where | Level 3 |
> | Prepare the Ground | a warded place: no surprise, no glamour; once a rest, a ward thrown down around you in a fight | Level 3 |
> | Cold Iron | 1d6 extra once a turn; 2d6 against the Hidden, who can't teleport away | Level 3 |
> | Inside Out | shrug off charm; give an ally a second try (Wisdom modifier plus Proficiency Bonus uses) | Level 7 |
> | Name It | pin a creature to the real for a round (spends a use of Inside Out); a ward the size of a village | Level 11 |
> | Iron Answer | shoot back when one of you is hit (spends a use of Inside Out) | Level 15 |
>
> **What it looks like:** the rider wearing your neighbour's face steps onto your ward, and the face comes off it. Your first arrow carries iron, and the rider can't flicker away from it. From 11th, you name the one leading them, and the whole party sees it pinned to the real.

**Not a Hidden Creature.** A Hidden Killer carries nothing of the Hidden, and keeps it that way.

features.name: Hidden Killer Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Hidden Killer Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Ranger Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Protection from Evil and Good* |
| 5 | *See Invisibility* |
| 9 | *Magic Circle* |
| 13 | *Banishment* |
| 17 | *Dispel Evil and Good* |

features.name: Read the Tide
features.text:
When you finish a Long Rest, or after you spend 10 minutes watching the land around you, you learn the following about the area within 1 mile of yourself:

- Whether the Hidden there are at the flood or at the ebb.
- Whether Hidden creatures are abroad in the area or gathering at its edge, roughly how many (a few, a band, or a Hunt), and the direction of the nearest of them.

You don't learn what they are. In addition, you don't have Disadvantage on Initiative rolls for being surprised by Hidden creatures, and you have Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track them. On your own border, any household gives you a meal and a bed when you ask, and tells you what it has seen since you last came by.

features.name: Prepare the Ground
features.text:
Anyone can iron and salt a room or a small building (see "Iron and salt" in "The Hidden, in the rules" in this book's introduction); a Killer's ward goes further.

You can spend 10 minutes warding a place against the Hidden: a building, or an area of open ground up to 60 feet on a side. You can do this during a Short or Long Rest. When you ward a place, choose any number of creatures the ward ignores (your allies, usually); the ward treats them as neither Hidden nor intruders. The ward lasts until you finish a Long Rest (a ward made during a Long Rest lasts until you finish the next one) or ward another place. It doesn't bar a Hidden creature from entering; iron and salt a door for that. While the ward lasts:

- **Forewarned.** You know when a creature the ward doesn't ignore enters it, and the knowledge wakes you if you're asleep. When combat starts and you or any of your enemies are in the ward, you and your allies have Advantage on Initiative rolls, and Hidden creatures in the ward that it doesn't ignore have Disadvantage on theirs.
- **No Glamour.** A Hidden creature in the ward that it doesn't ignore can't have the Invisible condition, and you and your allies see through any illusion or shape-changing effect that disguises such a creature there, seeing its true form alongside the false one. Such a creature can't teleport into or out of the ward.
- **Bread and Salt.** You and your allies have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed condition while in the ward.

**Nightmare Ward.** As a Magic action, you can throw down a ward where you stand: for 1 minute, a 10-foot Emanation from you is warded as above, though Forewarned has no effect, and it ignores you and your allies. It doesn't end a ward you've already made. Once you throw down a ward, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Cold Iron
features.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type to it. If the target is a Hidden creature, the extra damage is 2d6 instead, and it can't teleport until the start of your next turn.

In addition, while a creature is marked by your *Hunter's Mark*, you know whether it is a Hidden creature, it gains no benefit from the Invisible condition against you, and you see through any illusion or shape-changing effect that disguises it, seeing its true form alongside the false one.

features.name: Inside Out
features.text:
You have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed condition and on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to see through illusions, and magic can't make you lose your way.

When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw against the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to let it reroll the save; it must use the new roll.

You have a number of uses of Inside Out equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) plus your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Each reroll expends one. From 11th level, Name It spends the same uses, and from 15th, so does Iron Answer.

features.name: Name It
features.text:
When you hit a creature with a weapon and deal Cold Iron damage to it, you can name it. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a Hidden creature has Disadvantage on the save. On a failed save, it is pinned to the real until the end of your next turn: its Speed is 0, it can't teleport, become Invisible, or change its shape, and attack rolls against it have Advantage.

Each time you name a creature, expend one use of Inside Out.

**The Whole Village.** The ward you make with Prepare the Ground can now cover an area up to 300 feet on a side: a village, or the camp and the road through it.

features.name: Iron Answer
features.text:
When a creature you can see hits you or an ally with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to make one attack against it with a weapon you're holding, if it's within that weapon's range. You can deal Cold Iron damage with this attack, even though it isn't your turn and even if you've already dealt it this turn. Each Iron Answer expends one use of Inside Out.

> **Playing a Hidden Killer**
>
> A Killer's night starts before dark. Read the tide every morning, and when it tells you something is abroad, ward the place it will come to: the byre, the graveyard gate, the house with the new baby. On your own ground you go first, nothing hides, and the charm doesn't take. Caught off it, run for the gate, the bridge, or the friend the glamour is working on, and throw the ward down there. Off your ground you're still a Ranger with iron in every shot, and Cold Iron works on bandits and wolves as well as on the Hunt.
>
> Inside Out, Name It, and Iron Answer draw on one set of uses, and the day decides where they go: a friend coming back to themselves, or, from 11th, the Name that pins the thing the village sent you to kill.

data.name: Mortal Hunter
data.lead:
> **The Mortal Hunter at a Glance**
>
> **Take** is what a Mortal Hunter does. When a creature is Bloodied, or held by a condition, take it as a Bonus Action. If it fails a Wisdom saving throw, it vanishes from the fight; afterward it turns up asleep at your feet. Three uses a Long Rest, and you get one back on each Short Rest while the Hidden are at the flood.
>
> **Where you strike matters.** On thin ground, your prey saves at Disadvantage and can't find its way back unless a friend calls its name. If there's no thin ground, make some: spend a use of Take to call the mist.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | Of the Hunt | you know the tide and the open nights; you know thin ground | Level 3 |
> | Elf-Shot | 1d6 Psychic extra once a turn; your arrows can knock out | Level 3 |
> | Take | a Bloodied or held creature is taken out of the fight; spend a use to call the mist and make thin ground | Level 3 |
> | Pixie-Led | a hit on you misses on a failed save; you can't be lost or easily followed | Level 7 |
> | The Fairy Ride | the taken struggle to find their way back; the Hunt's road | Level 11 |
> | Will-o'-the-Wisp | Pixie-Led for your allies too | Level 15 |
>
> **What it looks like:** you came for one person, and your arrows find them. When they stagger, the mist closes and they are gone, and their friends are calling their name into the fog.

**A Hidden Creature.** A Mortal Hunter is a Hidden creature ("The Hidden, in the rules," in this book's introduction): it remembers what it is while it walks in the real world, and iron and salt bind it.

features.name: Mortal Hunter Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Mortal Hunter Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Ranger Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Sleep* |
| 5 | *Hold Person* |
| 9 | *Hypnotic Pattern* |
| 13 | *Confusion* |
| 17 | *Hold Monster* |

features.name: Of the Hunt
features.text:
You always know whether the Hidden are at the flood or the ebb where you are, and when the night ahead is an open night (the two in "The Hidden, in the rules," and any other night the DM says).

**Thin Ground.** You know thin ground when you're on it or can see it.

**The Hunt's Voice.** You can speak in the voice of anyone you have heard talk for a minute or more. Through a door or in the dark, people who know that voice take it for the person's own.

features.name: Elf-Shot
features.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can deal an extra 1d6 Psychic damage to it.

When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with an attack using a weapon, you can knock it out instead of killing it, even with a Ranged attack.

features.name: Take
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can try to take a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that is Bloodied or has the Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Incapacitated, Restrained, or Unconscious condition. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, with Disadvantage if it is on thin ground. On a failed save, it is **Taken** (Taken, in "The Hidden, in the rules," which also covers a creature someone is holding on to).

You can use this feature three times, whether or not the creature fails its save, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. While the Hidden are at the flood, you also regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest.

**Finding the Way.** At the end of each of its turns, a creature you Took repeats the save, and comes back on a success. On thin ground it can't find the way alone: it repeats the save only when a creature within 30 feet of the place it vanished from takes an action to call its name. If it is still Taken when combat ends or 1 minute has passed, it reappears asleep: it has the Unconscious condition in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you. It wakes after 1 hour, when it takes any damage (so the first hit wakes it), or when another creature takes an action to shake it awake. A sleeper can be bound or carried off, or woken to be bargained with.

**An Open Night.** When a creature you Took on an open night would reappear asleep, you can carry it into the Hidden instead. It returns when and where you choose, up to a year and a day later. For the taken, only a night has passed. The DM can rule that a creature of great power, or one the Hidden have reason to refuse, finds its own way back sooner.

**Call the Mist.** When you roll Initiative, or as a Magic action, you can expend one use of Take to call the mist: a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself is thin ground for 1 minute. The mist can't be called into a warded place.

**A creature that fights alone.** A creature with Legendary Resistance can use it on any save against Take. On thin ground, a Taken creature with no ally to call its name stays Taken until the fight ends, so one failed save can end a fight against a single great creature. Tell the DM before you try it. The DM can rule, as on an open night, that a creature of great power finds its own way back: it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, on any ground.

features.name: Pixie-Led
features.text:
When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll that isn't a Critical Hit, you can take a Reaction to lead it astray. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attack misses instead: it struck a wisp where you seemed to stand.

You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, you can't become lost except by magical means, and creatures have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track you or the creatures traveling with you.

features.name: The Fairy Ride
features.text:
A creature you Take anywhere but on thin ground has Disadvantage on the saves it repeats to find its way back.

When a Taken creature reappears asleep, you can have it reappear in an unoccupied space you have seen within 1 mile of where you took it, instead of near you.

In addition, you can lead up to six willing creatures onto the Hunt's road. For the next 8 hours, you and they travel at twice your normal travel pace and can't be tracked by nonmagical means. Any of you can leave the road at any time. Once you lead creatures onto the road, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Will-o'-the-Wisp
features.text:
You can use your Pixie-Led Reaction when a creature you can see hits a creature within 30 feet of you, as well as when it hits you.

> **Playing a Mortal Hunter**
>
> Shoot first, take second. Elf-Shot softens your prey for Take. The Hunt doesn't take the one already falling; it takes the one the village can't spare: the captain, the priest, the best shot on the wall. Your spells (*Sleep*, *Hold Person*, *Hypnotic Pattern*) put a condition on a creature still at full strength, and a held creature can be taken.
>
> The ground is the other half. Lead the prey onto thin ground before the fight, or call the mist as Initiative is rolled: there it saves at Disadvantage, and doesn't come back unless someone within 30 feet of where it vanished calls its name. A Hidden Killer's ward is never thin ground, and the mist can't be called into one.
>
> Watch the tide. At the flood you get a Take back every Short Rest. On an open night, what you take stays taken as long as you like, up to a year and a day; tell your DM before you try it on someone the story needs, because the DM can send a great power, or one the Hidden won't keep, home sooner.

data.name: Dreamlord Patron
data.lead:
*Take Them Under the Hill*

> **The Dreamlord at a Glance**
>
> **Step into the Hidden** is yours from 3rd level: cast, then step behind the world, and take a friend with you if one is beside you.
>
> **Spirited Away** comes at 6th. As a Bonus Action, a creature you can see makes a Charisma saving throw or the Hidden take it until the start of your next turn: out of the fight, its Concentration broken. A willing ally can choose to go.
>
> | Feature | What it does | From |
> |---|---|---|
> | Step into the Hidden | Bonus Action: teleport 30 feet, Invisible until your next turn; take a willing friend with you | Level 3 |
> | Manners | know whether a fae bargain binds; Advantage to bargain with Hidden creatures | Level 3 |
> | Spirited Away | a creature vanishes until your next turn | Level 6 |
> | Tracks of the Realm | see who has been to the Realm; know thin ground by touch | Level 6 |
> | Iron and Oaths | Immunity to Charmed; know when a promise to you breaks; know fairy gold by touch | Level 10 |
> | The Long Taking | keep a taken creature up to a minute; lead a party under the hill | Level 14 |
>
> **What it looks like:** the blow comes down on your friend, and your friend isn't there: you both stepped behind the world a moment before. From 6th, the brute about to swing is gone for a round, and comes back unsure where it has been.

**Not a Hidden Creature.** A Dreamlord Warlock bargains with the Hidden and carries nothing of it.

features.name: Dreamlord Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Warlock level specified in the Dreamlord Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Warlock Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Faerie Fire*, *Invisibility*, *Phantasmal Force*, *Sleep* |
| 5 | *Blink*, *Hypnotic Pattern* |
| 7 | *Dimension Door*, *Greater Invisibility* |
| 9 | *Dream*, *Seeming* |

features.name: Step into the Hidden
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you step out of the world and back in. You teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you have the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn. It ends early when you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell, and it doesn't give that attack roll Advantage.

**Come With Me.** When you Step into the Hidden, you can take one willing creature within 5 feet of yourself with you. It teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of where you arrive. It doesn't have the Invisible condition.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Manners
features.text: You know the Hidden's manners, and the near Realm's upside-down courtesies: which food a mortal can safely eat there and which binds them, which gifts are insults, how to accept hospitality and still leave. You always know whether a bargain a Hidden creature offers you is binding, and you have Advantage on Charisma checks to bargain with Hidden creatures.

features.name: Spirited Away
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail it. On a failed save, the Hidden take it: it is Taken (Taken, in "The Hidden, in the rules") until the start of your next turn, and it comes back early if you die or have the Incapacitated condition.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Tracks of the Realm
features.text: You can tell by looking at someone whether they've been to the Hidden Realm and come back, and whether they carry a piece of it (and so remember). By touching a door, a hill, a ring of mushrooms, or a standing stone, you know whether it's thin ground.

features.name: Iron and Oaths
features.text:
You have Immunity to the Charmed condition. In addition, when a creature breaks a promise it made to you (one it stated to you aloud, in a language you share), you know it at once, wherever it is.

**Fairy Gold.** By touching an object, you know whether it's mortal-made or fae (a Danae's fairy gold among them): gold that will be leaves by morning, a feast that's a table of bark and beetles, a letter that will be blank once it's read.

features.name: The Long Taking
features.text:
When a creature fails its saving throw against your Spirited Away, you can keep it Taken for up to 1 minute instead. At the start of each of your turns, it repeats the saving throw, coming back on a success. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**The Road Under the Hill.** You can take people into the Hidden. Standing on thin ground, you can spend 10 minutes opening the way, and you and up to eight willing creatures holding hands with you or with each other cross into the near reaches of the Hidden Realm. You return together to the place you left, when you choose or after 24 hours there; how much time has passed in the world is the DM's to decide. By default the same time passes in the world as under the hill; the DM can make it longer, and tells you before you go that it might be. Those who travel with you remember the journey, as if they'd brought a little of the Realm back with them, though none of them becomes a Hidden creature. Once you open the way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Dreamlord Warlock**
>
> You cast, then step behind the world: the Invisible condition lasts through the enemies' turns, and a spell cast after you step would end it. When a friend is about to be cut down, take them with you; they arrive beside you, visible but out of reach.
>
> Spirited Away takes a creature out of the world for a round: the enemy about to bring the roof down, or an ally about to take a blow they can't survive (an ally can choose to fail the save). Taking a caster ends its Concentration. A creature someone is holding can still be taken, but the holder can hold on (see Taken). Nothing of the Hidden is in you: Cold Iron's extra bite against the Hidden, the Iron Bell, and the wards that stop the Hunt don't touch you, and you deal with the Hidden as a guest, not as one of them.
